comparator.name: University College Maastricht
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 regulations, Articles 3.6–3.9 and Appendix I, govern the example. The single-domain template totals 180 EC: 20 EC core courses, 20 EC core skills and projects, 15 EC general education, 75 EC concentration courses, 15 EC concentration skills, 15 EC concentration projects and a 20 EC Capstone. The 15/75 split illustrates an allowed combination. A two-domain concentration requires Board of Examiners approval and has a separate general-education rule of 5–10 EC in the third domain. The catalogue supplies course content, sequencing and the 2.5 EC core skills credits. Appendix I controls the mandatory core, including COR1007. The catalogue also lists COR1006 as a core course and some skills text still references it, so the catalogue classification alone does not determine the required list.
components: Liberal Arts and Sciences Education in the 21st Century
This example uses three courses (15 EC) across the two domains outside a single concentration. The approved two-domain route instead requires one or two courses in the third domain.
This example uses fifteen courses (75 EC) in one domain. Concentration study combines introductory, intermediate and advanced work, including at least 20 EC of advanced coursework.
Choose six intermediate or advanced skills trainings under the concentration rules.
Choose three concentration projects, including at least one at advanced level.
Students complete this 20 EC final project after earning at least 140 EC.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Academic core: the four core topics every UCM student studies, namely how scientific research works and philosophy of science, modern political systems and political philosophy, scientific reasoning and its role in society, and key historical events of the past 75 years (Philosophy of Science, Contemporary World History, Political Philosophy, Liberal Arts and Science Education in the 21st Century)

Research methods, statistics and research training: Research Methods I and II, Introduction to Academic Skills, six concentration skills trainings (for example interviewing for academic research, systematic literature reviews, experimental methods) and research-oriented projects

Interdisciplinary liberal arts and sciences study: combining the social sciences, humanities and sciences, with general education outside the concentration and an optional interdisciplinary concentration, to investigate social and scientific problems from different perspectives
Social sciences domain: political science, international relations, international law, conflict studies, public policy and sociology, with quantitative and qualitative research methods
Humanities domain research: history and philosophy, with philosophical argument and analysis and research-based humanities projects such as documentaries
Sustainability, climate change and related evidence from natural systems, alongside social-science and humanities coursework.

Advanced concentration depth and independent research: a concentration with at least 20 EC of advanced courses over no fewer than three courses, advanced projects and a 20-EC Capstone research or analytical project
adjacent: Natural-science and behavioural research in psychology, cognitive neuroscience, biomedicine and population health.
Humanities domain: arts and literature, cultural studies and media studies as concentration directions, including research-based documentary work
Economics, business administration and international development as social-science concentration directions
Information and computer sciences and mathematics as science concentration directions
questions: How can complex social and scientific problems be investigated by combining academic disciplines and perspectives?
How do political systems, conflicts and the major historical events of recent decades shape contemporary societies?

trace: introduces central themes of Western philosophy, including the nature of knowledge, and the theoretical methods and argumentation philosophers use, relating them to psychology, law, physics and political science; it makes a specific contribution to the philosophical foundation of the academic core, although it is not a philosophy-of-science course

gives a chronological survey of modern history from 1815 to 2025 including the world wars, the Cold War and decolonisation; it directly implements the academic core's study of key historical events, over a longer period than the past 75 years

examines the views of influential Western thinkers on human nature, society and political authority and tests them against present political problems; it directly implements Political Philosophy in the academic core

studies human rights as positive law, in their history and in modern philosophy; it directly implements the international law direction and combines the legal and philosophical perspectives of the social-science and humanities domains

introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, descriptive and inferential statistics and analysis of variance; it directly implements the research methods and statistics training and the quantitative side of social-science research

develops data cleaning, visualisation and analysis on data sets from the sciences, social sciences and humanities and ends with an own research project; it directly implements quantitative analysis across the three domains of inquiry

surveys the history of warfare in the Western world from antiquity to nuclear arsenals, covering strategy, technology and guerrilla warfare; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the history direction and to the study of conflict

teaches the analytical tools for comparing political systems and the working of democracies, including democratic backsliding and the decline of political parties; it directly implements the political science direction and the academic core's study of modern political systems

introduces the concepts, methods and theories sociologists use to analyse societies from everyday interaction to global phenomena; it directly implements the sociology direction and is the foundation for the later sociology courses

examines law from legal, social and normative perspectives across constitutional, criminal, international and private law and the relation of law to society and justice; it directly implements the law component of the social-science domain and is the formal prerequisite of Introduction to Public International Law

examines the trajectory of sociology and theories of modernity within imperialism and colonial responses; it directly implements the sociology direction as the intermediate step between the introduction and advanced social theory

teaches virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism and applies them to practical questions such as climate change and historical injustice; it directly implements philosophical argument and analysis in the humanities domain

teaches qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation of social processes through a small team project; it directly implements the interviewing and qualitative research training of the skills trainings and the social-science research strand

presents the main schools of thought in international relations and applies them to historical and contemporary crises with a negotiation simulation; it directly implements the international relations direction

introduces the sources, subjects and organisation of public international law and its rules on the use of force, armed conflict, international criminal law, refugee law and environmental law; it directly implements the international law direction

covers the drivers of anthropogenic climate change, its impacts on natural systems and its consequences for society; it directly implements the sustainability and climate change direction as the scientific domain studied alongside the social sciences and humanities

teaches multivariate statistics including regression, factor analysis, ANOVA/ANCOVA and logistic regression for research on humans; it directly implements the statistics and quantitative analysis and experimental research training

engages with debates in contemporary social theory through civil society, solidarity, social capital and the public sphere, building on the introductory and modern sociology courses; it directly implements advanced sociology
analyses the institutions, actors and decision rules of the European Union and how its policies are made; it directly implements advanced political science and public policy analysis

examines theories of conflict causation, violence and peacebuilding drawing on history, sociology, political science, international relations and law; it directly implements the conflict studies direction at advanced level

traces the development of the documentary form and has students produce a short documentary, analysing non-fiction representations in their historical and social contexts; it makes a specific complementary contribution through media studies and the research-based documentary project UCM offers
has students write a substantial research paper using archival and historical methods; it directly implements humanities research and the advanced independent-research element of a concentration

examines how sustainability policies are made and enforced at local, national and international level and which actors shape them; it directly implements the public policy direction applied to sustainability and climate change

is the gateway to brain and behaviour, introducing psychological and neuroscientific approaches to why people behave as they do; it directly implements the psychology and cognitive science directions and is the prerequisite of the intermediate and advanced courses

teaches how cells, molecules and organ systems create and sustain life and health; it directly implements the biomedical science direction and is the prerequisite of the physiology, pathology and pharmacology courses
teaches epidemiology, how disease, risk and change over time are studied and how evidence for public health decisions is evaluated; it directly implements the global health direction
covers the main theories and findings on how feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by other people; it directly implements the psychology direction

studies the biological side of cognitive neuroscience, including evolutionary pressures, biorhythms, comparative anatomy and neurobiological disorders; it directly implements the cognitive science and neuroscience direction

examines consciousness, personal identity, the mind-body problem and whether the mind can be explained neurobiologically; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the cognitive science and neuroscience direction through the conceptual analysis of mind
gives the cellular and molecular biology foundation for medicine and the life sciences; it directly implements the biomedical science direction
teaches the normal function of the human body from molecules and cells to organ systems; it directly implements the biomedical science direction and the physiological basis for health
Examines attention, memory, emotion and other higher functions alongside the relevant brain systems and experimental evidence.
teaches the chemistry of life: proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids and metabolic pathways; it directly implements the biomedical science direction at intermediate level
explores the neural mechanisms of perception and action using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology; it directly implements the cognitive science and neuroscience direction
explores mental health and mental disorders across the lifespan from a bio-psycho-social perspective; it directly implements the psychology direction and connects psychology to health
explores human development across the lifespan, including cognitive and social development and ageing; it directly implements advanced psychology
covers the innate and adaptive immune response, host-pathogen interactions and disorders of the immune system; it directly implements advanced biomedical science

examines the biological, psychological and socio-cultural factors in health and illness and interventions in medical settings; it directly implements advanced psychology and connects it to global health
teaches the principles of pharmacology, drug targets, pharmacokinetics and toxicity; it directly implements advanced biomedical science
covers cell injury, inflammation, tissue repair and neoplasia together with the molecular genetics of human disease; it directly implements advanced biomedical science
Investigates psychosocial pathways into radicalisation, protective factors and interventions that support young people. It applies developmental and social psychology to resilience.
relates normal physiology to pathophysiology in six organ systems using clinical cases; it directly implements advanced biomedical science

teaches how to carry out systematic reviews and meta-analyses of research literature, including effect sizes and evidence-based policy; it directly implements the systematic-review research training that UCM offers in its skills trainings and the advanced research element
Applies blood analysis, aseptic technique and bacterial identification in laboratory work, strengthening the experimental life science strand after the biology gateway.
introduces psychological assessment, psychodiagnostics and psychotherapies in clinical psychology; it directly implements advanced psychology
introduces the interpretation of literary forms including novels, graphic narratives and film narration; it directly implements the arts and literature direction
gives a chronological overview of Western art history from the early Renaissance to the present; it directly implements the arts direction

studies rhetoric as it appears in political speech, social media and advertising and trains persuasive messages; it makes a specific complementary contribution to media and cultural studies through the analysis of public discourse
gives a chronological overview of major literary texts from the Epic of Gilgamesh to postmodernity and their themes; it directly implements the arts and literature direction

explores the histories and lives of people through the lens of gender in the United States from the nineteenth to the twenty-first centuries, drawing on cultural expression; it directly implements the cultural studies and history directions
examines how making objects shapes human societies and identities from early settlements to classical antiquity; it directly implements the cultural studies direction through material culture
introduces the history of cinema and how films work as an evolving cultural form; it directly implements the media studies direction

examines pre-digital media technologies such as typewriters, cassette tapes and early printed books and how they shaped knowledge; it directly implements the media studies direction through material and historical analysis
compares ancient and world myths and literary traditions across cultures; it directly implements the arts and literature and cultural studies directions
examines how audiovisual media represent and debate environmental issues, using concepts such as the Anthropocene and postcolonial media; it directly implements media studies and cultural studies
analyses memoir, autobiography, travel writing and blogs and develops writing and debating skills; it directly implements the arts and literature direction
examines social history and everyday life through American mainstream media from the mid-twentieth century to TikTok; it directly implements media studies and cultural studies
examines debates on modern art and how museums and exhibitions shape public perception; it directly implements advanced arts and cultural studies
analyses film adaptations of literary texts with interpretive strategies and cultural analysis; it directly implements advanced arts, literature and media studies
examines how film, photography and music address systemic racism and culminates in podcasts grounded in research; it directly implements advanced media and cultural studies

studies persuasion, framing and nudging through communication studies, social psychology and neuroscience, including climate communication; it makes a specific complementary contribution to media and cultural studies at advanced level

examines how humanist, feminist, Marxist, cultural-minority and psychoanalytic perspectives affect interpretation and has students carry out a research project on selected texts; it directly implements advanced literary research
Develops art-historical research, visual analysis and academic writing in the arts and culture sequence.
engages philosophical questions about emotions, rationality and well-being; it directly implements the philosophy strand of the humanities domain at advanced level

alternatives.label: Politics, Society and the Humanities
alternatives.labelReason: Explore how political institutions, law and social change shape contemporary societies. Use philosophy, history and social research methods to examine these questions, and study climate and sustainability from scientific and policy perspectives.
alternatives.concept: Explore how political institutions, law and social change shape contemporary societies. Use philosophy, history and social research methods to examine these questions, and study climate and sustainability from scientific and policy perspectives.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 6 level-300 courses. The current workbook confirms offerings and earlier formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Mind, Brain and Health
alternatives.labelReason: Study how the brain, behaviour and biological systems shape health. Build from psychology and life science to neuroscience, laboratory work, disease mechanisms, clinical psychology and systematic reviews.
alternatives.concept: Study how the brain, behaviour and biological systems shape health. Build from psychology and life science to neuroscience, laboratory work, disease mechanisms, clinical psychology and systematic reviews.
alternatives.distinctness: The mind, brain and health plan moves from introductory psychology and life science to laboratory methods, neurobiology, pathology and clinical psychology. It shares two courses with the politics and society plan and one with the literature and media plan.
traceOverrides: teaches multivariate statistics including regression, factor analysis and ANOVA/ANCOVA for research on human behaviour and health; it directly implements the experimental and statistical research training of the psychology direction and is the methods foundation of the Advanced Research Seminar
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 10 level-300 courses. The current workbook confirms offerings and earlier formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Literature, Media and Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Explore how literature, film, art and public communication shape cultural meaning. Combine interpretation with philosophy, history and qualitative research, and put media analysis into practice by making a documentary.
alternatives.concept: Explore how literature, film, art and public communication shape cultural meaning. Combine interpretation with philosophy, history and qualitative research, and put media analysis into practice by making a documentary.
alternatives.distinctness: The literature and media plan builds from interpretation of texts, images and objects to advanced literary and media research and documentary production. It shares five courses with the politics and society plan and one with the mind, brain and health plan.
traceOverrides: introduces central themes of Western philosophy and the theoretical methods philosophers use; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the philosophical foundation of the humanities concentration, alongside literary and cultural interpretation

teaches the main ethical theories and practical ethics including climate change and historical injustice; it makes a specific complementary contribution through the philosophical argument and analysis of the humanities domain

teaches qualitative research design and the interpretation of how people make sense of their world, and of how politics, history and cultures shape it; it directly supplies the interpretive research method for the cultural studies direction
traces the development of the documentary form and has students produce a short documentary; it directly implements media studies and the research-based documentary project UCM offers
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 8 level-300 courses. The current workbook confirms offerings and earlier formal prerequisites.

candidates.label: Psychology, cognitive science and neuroscience, biomedical science and global health (sciences domain)
Arts and literature, cultural studies and media studies (humanities domain)
Business administration, economics and international development (social-science domain)
Information and computer science and mathematics (science domain)

selection.assessment: Three coherent plans span distinct academic directions. Politics and society has the strongest overlap with the common core through history, political philosophy and academic methods and adds complementary climate and humanities study. Mind, brain and health takes the natural-science research and psychology directions into biomedical, behavioural and laboratory work. Literature and media develops humanities interpretation and research. Business, economics and development and computing and mathematics are coherent remaining directions outside the three-option limit. Curricular examples and graduate trajectories do not generate options.

blocks: Academic core: philosophy, history and political thought
Both study modern world history, including twentieth-century conflicts and political change. UCR surveys a longer period beginning in the nineteenth century.
Both study political thought and apply arguments about society and political authority to contemporary questions.
UCR’s introductory philosophy course explores knowledge and argument. Maastricht has a dedicated course on how scientific knowledge is produced and justified.
Academic skills, methods and research training
Both develop academic writing, argument and reflection on learning. The UCR course also covers personal and professional development.
Maastricht dedicates a core course to the purposes and practice of liberal arts and sciences education.
Both introduce research questions and study design. UCR adds statistical analysis, while Maastricht introduces qualitative and quantitative approaches.
Both develop qualitative research design and data collection. Maastricht uses this training to prepare a proposal for its linked Research Project.
Maastricht requires a separate project that develops academic inquiry and writing.
Maastricht requires a standalone first-year project following its two introductory methods trainings. UCR includes research projects within individual courses.
Maastricht requires a set of dedicated skills trainings. UCR develops methods through courses such as Qualitative Research Methodology and Statistics & Experimental Methods.
Maastricht requires three concentration projects. UCR develops related project skills in courses such as The Documentary and History Research Seminar.
Political science, international relations and law
Biomedical and life sciences and public health

notes.text: Maastricht combines a common academic core with general education and a chosen concentration. The UCR examples organise related interests around politics and society, mind and health, or literature and media.

Maastricht requires separate skills trainings, projects and a 20 EC Capstone. The UCR plans develop research skills within selected courses and show an optional independent research component separately.

audience.programmeDescription: University College Maastricht is an English-taught liberal arts and sciences bachelor. Students take a shared core and build depth in the humanities, social sciences or sciences. A concentration across two domains requires approval.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The politics and society option has the closest overlap with Maastricht’s common core in history, political philosophy and research methods. Two other UCR options explore established Maastricht interests in mind and health or literature and media. The comparison uses an example of Maastricht’s single-domain credit structure.
